conditions: Record must be a Linear issue (target of the priority update).
The issue must have a comment authored by a person named Priya.
That comment's content must be about an API timeout.
That comment must have been posted on September 22 (year unspecified).
The issue (or possibly the comment/thread, or the underlying problem) must have already been resolved by a person named Leo.
Exactly one issue should match all of the above (per 'the issue').
Action to perform: set the matched issue's priority to Urgent.

readings: The issue itself has already been resolved/closed by Leo (issue status change).
The comment/comment-thread posted by Priya was marked resolved by Leo.
The underlying API timeout problem was fixed by Leo, independent of any Linear status field.
September 22, 2026 (the most recent occurrence relative to today, 2026-09-26).
September 22 of some earlier year, if that's what the data reflects.

turn2.differences: The author's c1-c3 map directly onto my step-1 conditions covering the comment's author, topic, date, and resolution. The only thing left implicit by the author is that the target must be a single, uniquely-identified Linear issue, which is a trivial background assumption rather than a substantive gap.

ambiguity_effects.explain: Could mean the issue's workflow status was set to Done by Leo, or that Leo resolved the comment/thread via the resolvingUserId/resolvedAt fields. Under the issue-status reading, no issue in the workspace has ever reached Done, so nothing would match; under the comment-resolved reading, i-web-20 uniquely matches. The text alone leaves this open, though the data forces the comment-resolved reading in practice.
No year is stated for September 22. This is ambiguous in principle, but every relevant timestamp in the dataset is 2026, so there's no competing year to create a different match.

turn2.naturalness_note: Plausible as an over-specified request from someone disambiguating among similar tickets, though the trailing clause 'that Leo has already resolved' is dense and its antecedent (issue vs. comment) is unclear on a first read - a bit more constructed-feeling than typical spontaneous phrasing, but not implausible.
